subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for FinTrust PoC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fintrust.com>, John Lee <john.lee@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for FinTrust PoC

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our discovery:

Summary:
- Goal: Prototype onboarding assistant that summarizes secure transaction requests and highlights potential AML/OFAC flags.
- Primary constraints: low latency for web UI, strict PII redaction requirements, and explainability for flagged content.
- Expected volume: 5k–15k requests/day during PoC window.

Model fit notes (high level):
- For high-quality summarization with lower token cost, recommend trying a quantized 13B (Llama 3 / comparable) and a 33B curtailed variant for edge-case QA.
- We also have Redwood-verified small/medium models tuned for finance prompts (we can supply benchmark rows).

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Please send a sample of customer prompts/cases you want covered (happy-path and edge cases). CSV is fine — headers: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, sensitivity_tags.
2) Any internal redaction rules or categories (e.g., SSNs, account numbers, tokens we should mask).
3) Examples of failure modes you care about (false positives on AML flags, redaction misses, hallucinations).

Attachments: we commonly ask for a small prompt set to bootstrap evals — you can attach a CSV with examples.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll assemble a benchmark link with recommended prompt sets and baseline metrics (latency, token cost, quality per prompt).
- Rishi will scope minimal infra / autoscaling settings for your 5k–15k/day expectation.

If you can get the sample CSV and any redaction guidance by EOD Wed (Mar 11), we’ll turn around an initial eval report by the following Monday.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a sandbox.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Lee <john.lee@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 17:08:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for FinTrust PoC

Thanks, Marissa — helpful recap. Attaching a starter set of prompts we pulled from our support transcripts (sanitized). The CSV has ~25 rows; columns include a short context, the user utterance, and the expected agent summary.

Quick notes:
- We removed direct PII but left placeholders (e.g., <ACCOUNT_NUM>, <SSN_REDACTED>) so you can see where redaction should apply.
- Key categories to redact: SSN, full account numbers (keep last 4), DOB, account PINs, and internal customer IDs.
- Edge cases to flag: multi-account transfers, ambiguous beneficiary names, and third-party payment descriptions.

We have one legal question around storing prompt examples (even sanitized). Can you confirm Redwood’s handling for PoC data and whether the uploads are retained beyond the evaluation?

Attaching: fintrust_prompt_examples.csv

Regards,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Product Manager, Fraud Prevention | FinTrust Bank
alicia@fintrust.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fintrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:03:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for FinTrust PoC

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the CSV — looks great as a starting set. A few clarifying items and what we’ll provide in the eval: 

Clarifications needed from you:
- For masked placeholders: do you want us to treat <ACCOUNT_NUM> as full PII to be removed from logs, or masked and retained for context (last 4 visible)? Please indicate per tag.
- For third-party payment descriptions: any vendor list or pattern rules we should prioritise?

What we’ll deliver by Mon, Mar 16 (initial eval):
- Benchmark report (CSV/Drive) with per-prompt quality scores (BLEU/ROUGE-style + human labels), latency percentiles, and estimated token cost across 3 model candidates. Link will include raw outputs and evaluation notes.
- Recommended model profiles: 
  * rdw-llama3-13b-quant (recommended start: best balance of quality/cost)
  * rdw-rlhf-33b-safety (for high-sensitivity or high-precision flagging; higher cost)
  * rdw-compact-7b (if latency is primary and you can accept modest quality drop)
- A short note on quality regression detection: we’ll create a baseline eval set from your CSV + 40 synthesized edge cases; we’ll run nightly checks and flag regressions when quality drops >8% on priority prompts.

Security / data retention answer: For PoC uploads we keep artifacts in an isolated S3 bucket with a PoC lifecycle policy (30 days) unless you request longer retention. We can commit to not using data for training outside the scope of the PoC and enable a delete workflow post-eval. I’ll have Rishi follow up with a quick note on retention config and audit logs.

Can you confirm per-placeholder redaction preference by EOD Wed so we don’t generate a baseline that violates policy?

--
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Lee <john.lee@fintrust.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:44:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for FinTrust PoC

Got it — confirmed: treat <SSN_REDACTED> and <ACCOUNT_NUM> as PII that should not be stored in identifiable form. For <ACCOUNT_NUM> we can provide last4 in a separate non-identifying column if you need it for matching.

We’ll also export an additional 40 edge cases (including multi-account, suspicious memo text, and mixed-language descriptions) and upload to the same Drive link before EOD Wed.

Legal is okay with 30-day retention for the PoC provided we have the delete workflow documented and the bucket is isolated. Please include a short retention clause in the SOW.

Thanks — sending the extra prompts shortly.

Regards,
Alicia
